qt: to the Commission Marcin Sypniewski (ESN) Subject:

In 2026, irregularities came to light concerning EU imports of Brazilian beef from cattle treated with oestradiol 17β, a substance not authorised for use as a growth promoter in EU livestock farming. According to publicly available reports, roughly 63 tonnes of this beef entered the EU, while a further 25 or so tonnes were intercepted in the Netherlands. This affair raises questions not only about the effectiveness of EU import controls, but also about what became of the meat that had already been placed on the market. In light of the above: 1.

Can the Commission provide a full account of the beef in question, broken down by Member State and specifying the exact quantities seized, withdrawn from the market, destroyed and released for human consumption?
Has it been established how much of this meat was consumed before the affected consignments were identified, and if so, what volume was involved and in which countries was it placed on the market?

What additional inspection measures have been imposed on Brazilian exporters and Brazil’s competent authorities in the wake of this incident, and how effective have they proved to be in the Commission’s view?
